text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — dedicated pool 'orchidhealth-prod' GPU utilization 100% (queuing increasing). latency p95 > 3s, error spike. paging oncall
maria (oncall-sre): on it, grabbing metrics. what's the current queue length?
mike (eng-runtime): seeing heavy KV cache churn + long stalls in attention kernels. logs: `rvw_serving: req_wait=142s, gpu_util=100%`
sasha (dedicated-ops): orchidhealth is a single-tenant dedicated pool, autoscale policy is conservative (max_nodes=8, burst_allowed=false). they have an SLA but not unlimited burst.
sam (cs): pinging lucy on customer side. Lucy, can you confirm if they kicked off a big batch export?
lucy (customer-success): yes they started a nightly embeddings backfill at ~00:20 UTC, didn't notify Ops. They're seeing timeouts on their end.
maria (oncall-sre): severity = sev2 (customer-facing latency, single tenant). immediate mitigation options: 1) enable burst to shared pool (risk noisy neighbors), 2) temporarily throttle customer's QPS, 3) add nodes to dedicated pool (slow, requires infra ops + billing). thoughts?
mike (eng-runtime): technical note: we can trigger ephemeral burst by flipping `enable_shared_burst=true` for that tenant in control-plane. runtime will spin up g4dn instances in ~90s but they'll be unquantized and cost > dedicated. alternative: switch customer's model to a quantized variant or smaller model if customer tolerates lower quality — that cuts GPU pressure ~40%.
sasha (dedicated-ops): I can update autoscale to max_nodes=12 immediately via the control plane API, but provisioning will still take ~3-6 minutes. burst flip is faster.
maria (oncall-sre): cost vs customer impact — customer experiencing errors now. recommend: 1) enable burst for 30 minutes, 2) set tenant throttling to 50% for non-critical routes, 3) notify customer. Agree?
sam (cs): Lucy, propose we enable burst while they pause the backfill for the next hour. They'll approve.
lucy (customer-success): they approve enabling burst. also asked to credit them for spike.
maria (oncall-sre): @sasha can you flip burst and add a per-tenant soft-rate-limit rule? please include a kill-switch.
sasha (dedicated-ops): executing now. API call: ```
# enable shared burst for tenant
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/tenants/orchidhealth/actions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -d '{"action":"enable_shared_burst","duration_minutes":30}'
```
deploy-bot: action accepted — enabling burst for tenant orchidhealth (request id 01F8X).
sasha (dedicated-ops): adding soft QPS throttle rule: `tenant.orchidhealth.qps_soft_limit=200` and `route:/v1/embeddings->priority=high`
mike (eng-runtime): watching metrics — GPU queue length dropping, p95 latency improving. current GPU util ~78% and falling.
maria (oncall-sre): @mike can you confirm KV cache hit rates?
mike (eng-runtime): KV hit improved from 12% -> 36% after burst nodes came up, but note increased egress from shard sync.
sam (cs): Customer confirms success, requests we keep them stable for next 45min while they finalize.
maria (oncall-sre): marking incident paged -> active mitigation. I've informed product and account team.
lucy (customer-success): thanks — they'll stop the backfill now. asking for follow-up doc and credits.
sasha (dedicated-ops): burst will auto-disable at +30min; I'll monitor. setting alert to notify if queue > 50 for >2min.
maria (oncall-sre): handoff: I'm on call until 03:00 UTC, then @mike will take over for the observation window. tagging follow-ups: - runbook update for dedicated-pool burst playbook, - add scheduled-job warning to CS onboarding, - investigate autoscale smoothing so we can react faster.
mike (eng-runtime): noted for handoff. also recommend a model fallback strategy: add a lower-cost quantized variant to tenant model catalog and enable automatic fallback when queue > 60.
sasha (dedicated-ops): postmortem action: consider default burst=true for enterprise pools with opt-out. will draft a proposal.
maria (oncall-sre): final status: mitigation successful, customer-stable, incident -> monitoring. severity downgraded to sev3 for tracking. filing incident ticket.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — 2367801234 status=mitigated, assigned=maria. next steps: postmortem, billing review, runbook updates.
deploy-bot: control-plane action log: `enable_shared_burst orchidhealth by sasha at 2367801299`, `qps_policy set by sasha at 2367801310`
sam (cs): I'll coordinate customer credits and get signoff from finance.
maria (oncall-sre): quick RCA notes in thread: root cause = uncoordinated large nightly backfill + conservative autoscale caps; contributing factor = no scheduled-job alerting for dedicated pools.
mike (eng-runtime): adding TODO: instrument per-tenant scheduled-job detection and an early-warning alarm for sustained enqueue > 60s.
sasha (dedicated-ops): logging: `orchidhealth_pool: max_nodes_before=8, after=12, burst_enabled=true`
lucy (customer-success): customer asks for a short summary doc and confirmation of credits. I'll draft and share.
maria (oncall-sre): thanks all. I'll close monitoring when 30m expire and metrics stable for 15m. leaving this thread open for now. :white_check_mark:
